tasks.title: Section A: Air transport and greenhouse gases
tasks.statement: Resource A1 shows the primary greenhouse gases (dynamics, longevity and potential impact). Resource A2 shows the carbon dioxide emissions from air travel in the world by country in 2018. Resource A3 shows the number of air passengers in Europe in 2019 by country.

parts.question: Study Resource A1. Define the term greenhouse effect.
parts.reference:
Award 2 marks for a complex explanation that contains at least four of the following elements:
• short-wave radiation (visible light from the Sun)
• heating of the Earth’s surface
• long-wave (infrared) radiation emitted from Earth’s surface
• greenhouse gases in the atmosphere that trap the heat
• emitting the trapped heat back toward Earth’s surface

Award 1 mark for a simple explanation that contains at least two elements listed above.
Accept any other relevant and correct answer.

parts.question: Study Resource A1. Outline three impacts of selected greenhouse gases on climate change.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for each outlined effect accompanied by specific statistical evidence.
Award 0.5 mark for a listed effect without specific evidence.
Accept any other relevant and correct answer.

parts.question: Study Resource A2. Name the countries that have the highest carbon footprints in international and domestic air travel.
parts.reference:
USA (0.5 marks)
China (0.5 marks)

parts.question: Study Resource A2. Outline two reasons why some countries have very high carbon dioxide emissions per capita from domestic air travel.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for each correct reason.
Only one answer can relate to size or shape of the country (first three bullets).
Accept any other relevant and correct answer.

parts.question: In addition to carbon dioxide, other greenhouse gases and aerosols are emitted from air transport. Explain the effect of condensation trails on climate.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for the explanation of condensation trails that contains at least two of the following elements:
• line-shaped clouds
• condensed water
• produced by the combustion of aviation fuel
(Award 0.5 mark for an answer that contains only one of these elements)

Award 1 mark for the explanation of effect of condensation trails on climate that contains at least two of the following elements:
• absorption of long-wave (infrared) radiation from Earth’s surface
• preventing cooling effect
• reflecting long-wave radiation back to Earth’s surface
• effect similar to clouds
(Award 0.5 mark for an answer that contains only one of these elements)
Accept any other relevant and correct answer.

parts.question: Study Resource A3. Use an appropriate data representation method to display the total number of passengers in air travel and their profile (national and international passengers) in European countries with more than 50 million total passengers.
parts.reference:
Award 2 marks for appropriate diagram. It can be vertical or horizontal. Do not award any marks for any other type of diagram.

Award 2 marks only for a diagram with values ordered from highest to lowest (or vice versa), with no empty space on axes and drawn using a ruler (or precisely by hand).
• 0.5 mark is subtracted if values are not ordered from highest to lowest (or vice versa)
• 0.5 mark is subtracted if there in empty space on x/y axis with no values
• 0.5 mark is subtracted if the diagram is not drawn using a ruler or very precisely by hand
• 0.5 mark is subtracted if values are not plotted accurately

Award 0.5 marks for each of the following elements that have been drawn correctly:
• 0.5 mark for suitable title (must have reference to air passengers /in European countries/) and “2019”
• 0.5 mark for the names of the countries on the x axis (or y axis on the bar diagram)
• 0.5 mark for the label “Number of passengers” or “Number” on the y axis (or x axis on the bar diagram)
• 0.5 mark for accurately displayed values on y axis (or x axis)
• 0.5 mark for expressing national and international passengers in a different way (e.g. different colours)
• 0.5 mark for a legend that contains colour and name of each displayed category

tasks.title: Section B: South Pacific Ocean
tasks.statement: A 2016 animated movie “Moana“, produced by Walt Disney, tells the story of a strong-willed girl, Moana, who lives in a Polynesian village. Since the location of this story is set in the South Pacific Ocean, many unique geographic features can be found in this movie. Resource B1 shows a rock type ‘A’ and a water body ‘B’. Resource B2 shows the climate data for an island in the South Pacific Ocean. Resource B3 shows the global distribution of natural hazards. Resource B4 shows the international arrivals of overnight and same day visitors to various places in the world in 2008 and 2018.

parts.question: Study Resource B1. Identify the type of rock represented by ‘A’.
parts.reference: Basalt

parts.question: Study Resource B1. Identify the type of water body represented by ‘B’.
parts.reference: Lagoon

parts.question: An atoll is a unique feature in the South Pacific Ocean. With the use of an annotated diagram, explain clearly how an atoll is formed.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for each bullet point:
- Drawing is in correct order of formation of an atoll
- Evidence of volcanic island surrounded by coral reef
- Volcanic island sinks and coral reef grows upward
- Volcanic island disappeared and coral reef becomes an atoll

parts.question: Study Resource B2. Identify the climate type of the island in the South Pacific Ocean using the Köppen climate classification.
parts.reference: Tropical Monsoon climate OR Am climate

parts.question: Study Resource B3. Explain two natural hazards occurring in the South Pacific Ocean which might affect the local economies of the South Pacific Ocean islands.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for each natural hazard. Maximum of 2 marks to be awarded.
Award 1 mark for explanation on how each natural hazard affects the local economies of the South Pacific Ocean islands. Maximum of 2 marks to be awarded.
Maximum of 4 marks to be awarded. Accept any other relevant answer.

parts.question: Study Resource B4. To what extent do you agree that tourism is beneficial for the Pacific Least Developed Countries (LDCs)?
parts.reference:
Award 4 marks if answer shows both benefits and disadvantages of tourism for the Pacific LDCs and is well-explained.
Award 3 marks if answer shows both benefits and disadvantages but might lack elaboration for one or more points.
Award 2 marks if answer is only focused on benefits OR disadvantages.
Award 1 mark if answer is only focused on benefits OR disadvantages but lacks elaboration.
Award 0 marks if answer is irrelevant.

tasks.title: Section C: Lower Mekong Basin
tasks.statement: Resource C1 shows the map of the Mekong Basin. Resource C2 shows the average wet season precipitation in the Mekong Basin in 2019, as compared to 2000-2018. Resource C3 shows the satellite image of part of the Mekong River in Thailand in 2015 and 2020. Resource C4 shows future scenarios (i.e. B1, M1 and M3) for land subsidence in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta between 2030 and 2100. Resource C5 shows the Vietnamese government’s future vision for the sustainable development of the Mekong Delta. This plan was developed in consultation with the Dutch government.

parts.question: Study Resources C1 and C2. Describe the average wet season precipitation in the Mekong Basin in 2019, as compared to 2000-2018.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for each of the following:
- Drier than usual weather occurring in Mekong basin of Cambodia, Lao – or in the majority of the Mekong Basin
- Average precipitation occurring in Mekong basin of China, eastern Thailand/SW Laos and southernmost of Vietnam
- Wetter than usual weather occurring mostly at upstream section of Mekong in China, just after mid-way of the Mekong river in China, eastern Thailand/SW Laos and southernmost of Vietnam
Maximum of 3 marks to be awarded.

parts.question: Study Resource C3. Describe the change(s) observed in this part of the Mekong River in Thailand between 2015 and 2020.
parts.reference:
Award 0.5 marks for the following:
- The colour of the Mekong River changed from muddy brown to blue; or less sediment in the river
- Loss of vegetation cover
Maximum of 1 mark to be awarded.

parts.question: Study Resource C3. Explain two reasons to account for the change(s) observed in this part of the Mekong River in Thailand between 2015 and 2020.
parts.reference: Award 1 mark for each reason to explain colour change OR loss of vegetation cover. Students must explain both colour change and loss of vegetation cover to get maximum of 2 marks.

parts.question: Study Resource C4. Explain the relationship between groundwater extraction and land-subsidence.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for:
- More groundwater extraction leads to more land subsidence

parts.question: Study Resource C4. Explain which scenario is likely to be the most sustainable scenario for the Vietnamese Mekong Delta.
parts.reference: Award 2 marks for each chosen scenario which is well explained.

parts.question: Study Resource C4. Explain which scenario is likely to be the most realistic scenario for the Vietnamese Mekong Delta.
parts.reference: Award 2 marks for each chosen scenario which is well explained.

parts.question: Study Resource C5. Choose two solutions shown in Resource C5 and explain how each of them could help the Vietnamese Mekong Delta be sustainable.
parts.reference: Award maximum of 2 marks for each chosen solution which is well explained. Maximum of 4 marks to be awarded.

tasks.title: Section D: Wildfires, sinking cities and sustainable development
tasks.statement: Resource D1 shows the top 20 largest wildfires in California, USA. Resource D2 shows the distribution of population density growth projections and fire hazards in California. Resource D3 shows the risk to selected Asian cities due to rising sea levels and flooding by 2030. Resource D4 shows the Sustainable Development Goals as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

parts.question: Study Resource D1. Explain how wildfires can be caused by both human and natural factors.
parts.reference: Award 2 marks for each well-explained factor. Students must explain both human and natural factors to be awarded 4 marks.

parts.question: Study Resource D2. Compare the distributions of population density growth projections and fire hazards in California.
parts.reference:
Award 1 mark for each of the following:
• High wildfire hazard leads to very low population growth
• Southern California: areas surrounding Los Angeles are high hazard areas but still attract population.

parts.question: Study Resource D3. Describe the severity of risks to the selected Asian cities due to rising sea levels and flooding.
parts.reference: Award 1 mark each for any 2 of the provided valid points from the marking guide.

parts.question: Study Resource D3. Choose a city in Resource D3 and explain two strategies it can adopt to increase overcome the risk of flooding.
parts.reference: Award 1 mark for each well-explained strategy which is related to the city of choice.

parts.question: Study Resource D4. In your opinion, are wildfires or floods more damaging towards a city’s pursuit of sustainable development? Explain your choice.
parts.reference:
Reserve and award 1 mark for the definition of sustainable development or sustainable urban development. A 5 marks answer will include the definition AND meet the criteria to be awarded 4 marks. If students do not define the term, answer will receive a maximum of 4 marks.
Award 4 marks if answer shows understanding of how both wildfires and floods can affect sustainable development but presents argument on how one of them is more damaging than the other.
Award 3 marks if answer shows slight understanding but argument is weak.
Award 2 marks if answer only focuses on wildfires or floods.
Award 1 mark if answer is descriptive.
Award 0 marks if irrelevant.

tasks.title: Section E: Green Revolution and Population Development
tasks.statement: Resource E1 shows the global change in population development, cereal production, cereal yield and land use from 1961 to 2021. Resource E2 shows contemporary farming occurring in Bangladesh.

parts.question: Define the ‘Green Revolution’.
parts.reference:
Award 1m for a concept/technique applied in agriculture shifting to industrial practice based on advanced technology to increase crop yield.
Award 1m for mentioning at least 3 characteristics (chemical inputs, heavy farm mechanization, managed irrigation, high yielding varieties, etc.).

parts.question: Study Resource E1. Describe the trends observed.
parts.reference: Award 0.5 marks for each correct trend described from the list in the official marking guide.

parts.question: Using your own knowledge, outline Thomas Malthus’ theory on the concept of “population-resources” relationship.
parts.reference: Award 1 mark each for at least 2 valid points regarding Malthus' theory.

parts.question: Using your own knowledge, outline Ester Boserup’s theory on the concept of “population-resources” relationship.
parts.reference: Award 1 mark each for at least 2 valid points regarding Boserup's theory.

parts.question: Study Resource E2. Suggest three ways in which farmers in Bangladesh have benefitted differently from the Green Revolution.
parts.reference: Award 1 mark each for any 3 of the listed points in the marking guide.

parts.question: Using your own knowledge, explain two ways in which agricultural practices can be improved to allow countries to benefit more.
parts.reference: Award 2 marks for each well-explained measure. Award only 1 mark if not explained enough. Zero marks if simply stated without explanation.
